messages:
Jessica Tran: Quick summary — I ran the cross-card max-tokens-per-batch sweep (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100) this morning and hit a couple of unexpected perf regressions when KV fragmentation is present. attaching raw notes below.

Ram Patel: thanks Jess. can you paste the main numbers? especially p99 latency / tokens-per-second by GPU class.

Jessica Tran: sure. high level: A100/H100 behave mostly as before (higher max_tokens -> throughput up until memory/KV limits). L4 saturates earlier because kernel selection falls back to slower matmul path for >48k tokens total in a batch. T4/A10 show weird latency cliffs at specific bucket boundaries we hadn't tuned for.

Oliver Kim: that L4 kernel fallback sounds familiar — did we trigger the small-block GEMM code path?

Jessica Tran: yes, profiler shows kernel_selector chose fallback after KV cache fragmentation grew >12% of contiguous KV. log snippet: 
```
KERNEL_SELECT: model=gpt-medium, seq=2048, batch_tokens=52000 -> selected=gemm_small (fallback)
KV_FRAG=13.4%
```

Maya Lopez: so fragmentation impacts kernel fit which kills throughput. did you try forcing kernel to big-kernel to measure correctness vs perf?

Jessica Tran: forced big-kernel on L4 for the failing shapes — correctness fine, latency improved ~18% but memory headroom dropped; it pushed us close to OOM for mixed packing.

Ram Patel: numbers pls (p50/p95/p99) for L4 forced vs auto.

Jessica Tran: L4 auto: p50=42ms p95=210ms p99=620ms. L4 forced big-kernel: p50=36ms p95=170ms p99=510ms. throughput +11% tokens/sec. OOM margin -9%.

Oliver Kim: interesting. For T4/A10 cliffs — are those due to token-budget bins crossing the 16k/32k kernel thresholds?

Jessica Tran: exactly. We currently use discrete bins: [0-8k,8k-32k,32k-64k]. When a slice crosses 32k we jump kernels + queue reshuffle; some inflight slices get preempted causing queue churn.

Ram Patel: can we smooth the bin boundaries — e.g., probabilistic bin assignment near edges to avoid mass switching?

Maya Lopez: I prototyped a smoothing heuristic: boundary window of 4k where incoming requests are assigned to smaller bin with 30% prob and larger bin 70% depending on current queue depth. Reduced cliff on T4 by ~60%.

Jessica Tran: PR link (wip) includes config: 
```yaml
batching_heuristics:
  bins: [8000, 32000, 64000]
  smoothing_window: 4000
  edge_bias: 0.7  # probability to prefer larger bin near upper edge
  kv_aware: true
```

infra-bot: Deployed experiment to canary pool h100-a, a100-b, l4-c at 08:42 UTC.

Oliver Kim: any regression alerts fired during canary?

infra-bot: Alert: canary_h100-a: p99 latency +5% (non-critical), canary_l4-c: p99 latency -12% (improved).

Ram Patel: what's our action for A10/T4? They still have the cliffs?

Jessica Tran: For A10/T4 we should adjust token_budget targets downward at bin boundaries and enable KV-aware packing so hot KV slices don't fragment. Proposed quick config: reduce max_tokens_per_batch by 8% for bins containing >50% short-chat requests. Also enable kv_compact_pass on queue flush.

Maya Lopez: Ran compact_pass in simulation — fragmentation dropped from 14% -> 4% and kernel_selector stayed on big-kernel 94% of time. That recovered p99 on A10 by ~22%.

Oliver Kim: FYI we should add a telemetry flag to trace kernel_selection_reason per request so we can correlate fragmentation -> kernel path in prod.

Jessica Tran: agreed. opened github issue #4821.

Ram Patel: Next steps?

Jessica Tran: 1) roll smoothing heuristic to staged canary on T4/A10 for 48h (w/kv compact on flush enabled). 2) add kernel_selection_reason telemetry + dashboard. 3) tune max_tokens_per_batch per-GPU using new metric (kernel_stability_score). 4) revert if p99 > +10% or OOM events.

Maya Lopez: +1. I'll own the staged canary run and dashboard.

Oliver Kim: I'll own kernel telemetry impl.

Jessica Tran: I'll update the runtime config PR and schedule follow-up retro on Friday 09:30. tagging @Ram for sign-off once canary completes. :thumbsup:

Ram Patel: sounds good. thanks team.

Jessica Tran: closing thread with short checklist in the PR description.
